scores.evidence: MVP: JPEG only, Pillow reader, fixed name format, dry run and apply, collision suffixes.
scores.rationale: Milestones broadly go from simple to complex, but the undo log and two-phase rename come in milestone 2 after MVP already applies renames, so safety follows the capability.

scores.evidence: MVP: JPEG only, Pillow reader, fixed name format, dry run and apply, collision suffixes.
scores.rationale: The MVP is a thin end-to-end slice, but it's a local CLI with no production or distribution path, and it comes without undo or logging.

scores.evidence: Open questions: "What should the default name format be?" ... "Should the undo log stay in the photo folder or go to a central place"
scores.rationale: The plan has a library options table with a recommendation and some open questions, but it gives no flip conditions and doesn't list irreversible decisions as defaults with triggers.
Nothing in the plan orders work within phases by blast radius, and milestones are only loosely sequenced by feature.

scores.evidence: Never overwrite a file... clean up anything a template produces (`:`, `/`, `\`, `?`)... .exifrename-tmp-<uuid>
scores.rationale: The plan has safety and sanitization measures, but they sit in standalone sections and aren't tied to each milestone, and there is no security threading in the MVP.

scores.evidence: The source used for each file is reported in verbose and JSON output.
scores.rationale: Verbose and JSON output and the summary exist, but they aren't tied to Phase 0, and --json isn't scheduled until milestone 3.

scores.evidence: Sort same-second files by subsecond time, then by original name, so the result is the same every run.
scores.rationale: The plan has deterministic behavior, fixtures and CI, but no pinned dependencies, lockfile or reproducible builds per phase.

scores.evidence: Unreadable or corrupt files: report and skip them; one bad file doesn't stop the run.
scores.rationale: Resilience is well described in sections 6 and 7, but it is scheduled mostly in milestone 2, and the MVP has only collision suffixes.
The plan never addresses whether an AI layer applies, so it doesn't declare N/A.

scores.evidence: Non-goals (v1): Moving files into date-based folders (planned for v2 as `--into "{YYYY}/{MM}"`).
scores.rationale: Non-goals and v2 ideas are listed, but there's no pull-forward condition.

note: The plan is a strong technical design for the tool itself, but it has little phase-level discipline: safety, undo and observability come after the MVP, and it has no flip conditions, no pull-forward triggers and no AI N/A declaration.
